question: Which of the following acid-base indicators is colourless in acidic medium and pink in basic medium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Phenolphthalein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is a synthetic chemical compound often used as an **acid-base indicator** in laboratories.
 
• In an **acidic medium**, phenolphthalein remains completely **colourless**. It also remains colourless in **neutral** solutions.
 
• When the solution becomes **basic** (alkaline), phenolphthalein molecules undergo a structural change, resulting in a vibrant **pink** or **magenta** colour.
 
• The **pH transition range** for phenolphthalein is typically between **8.2 and 10.0**. Below **pH 8.2**, it is colourless, and above **pH 10.0**, it is pink.
 
• It is widely utilized in **analytical chemistry**, particularly during **titrations** involving a **strong base** and a **weak acid**, to accurately identify the end point of the reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Litmus**: 
 
 
• It is a **natural indicator** extracted from **Lichens**.
 
• In an **acidic medium**, litmus paper or solution turns **red**, while in a **basic medium**, it turns **blue**.
 
• A **neutral** litmus solution is **purple** in colour.
 
 
 
• **Methyl Orange**: 
 
 
• This is a **synthetic indicator** used for titrations involving strong acids.
 
• It exhibits a **red** colour in **acidic** solutions (below **pH 3.1**) and a **yellow** colour in **basic** or **neutral** solutions (above **pH 4.4**).
 
• In the transition range, it appears **orange**.
 
 
 
• **Bromothymol Blue**: 
 
 
• It is a chemical indicator for weak acids and bases. It appears **yellow** in **acidic** conditions, **green** in **neutral** conditions, and **blue** in **basic** conditions.
 
• Its **pKa** is approximately **7.1**, making it useful for reactions occurring near **neutral pH**.
 
 
 
• **Natural Indicators**: 
 
 
• **Turmeric**: Remains **yellow** in **acid** but turns **reddish-brown** in a **base**.
 
• **China Rose** (Hibiscus): Turns **dark pink (magenta)** in **acidic** solutions and **green** in **basic** solutions.
 
 
 
• **Olfactory Indicators**: These are substances like **onion**, **vanilla essence**, and **clove oil** whose **odour** changes depending on whether they are mixed with an **acid** or a **base**.
